mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate used in equity valuation models, leading to higher present values of future cash flows and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is negative in more than 60% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 6.5%, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low industrial production (INDPRO < 90.0), manufacturing slowdowns reduce corporate profits and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0, or the average return in the regime is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is negative in more than 60% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between PAYEMS and UNRATE fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 550.0 thousand units, it signals weak residential demand and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 550.0, or the average 5-day return in the regime is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
